completion_verdict.schema.json:21 defines evidence_sufficient=false as 'the bounded evidence search was exhausted without finding evidence and NOTHING was positively refuted' — the same shape as zero-banking, differing only in count (0 vs >=1 records).
_insufficiency_only (completion.py:511-520) already classifies an all-insufficiency FAIL; a zero-record bank is the count=0 edge of that same predicate.
findings.finding: AC1 draws a hard ERROR-vs-FAIL boundary between zero-banked and partial-bank exhaustion without justifying why zero banks is a gate FAULT while one insufficiency bank is a completion JUDGEMENT — both are 'search exhausted, nothing positively refuted'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the ordering/atomicity of the stale-snapshot guard: define exactly when the pin and the compared store HEAD are captured (same instant / same read) so a legitimate concurrent store advance between pin and check is not misreported as a stale-snapshot ERROR.
evidence: Fix item 4 compares the pin against 'the store HEAD read at run start' — but 2a6f's fix already pins the tracker HEAD at the live store's own HEAD by construction (repo_snapshot materialize_tickets), so a mismatch can only arise if the HEAD read and the pin are taken at different instants.
If the store advances between the pin and the run-start HEAD read (a normal concurrent commit), the guard fires ERROR even though the snapshot is internally consistent and signable.
findings.finding: The stale-snapshot guard (fix #4) asserts pin==store-HEAD-at-run-start but the plan does not pin the ordering of the pin vs. the HEAD read, so the check can be a TOCTOU that spuriously flags legitimate mid-run store advancement as ERROR.
findings.location: Fix item 4 ('assert the pinned ticket snapshot's event count/status matches the store HEAD read at run start')
scenarios: Concurrent ticket activity (another agent commits a comment) between pin and the guard's HEAD read → the verifier reports ERROR (stale) for a snapshot that is actually a valid immutable pin, converting a benign race into a retry loop.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare the pin against the HEAD used to CREATE the pin (i.e. assert the snapshot equals the state materialize_tickets pinned), not a fresh live-HEAD read taken later — since 2a6f already pins at live HEAD by construction, the invariant to assert is 'the fenced-context read and the model's show_ticket read agree with the pin', which detects the 2a6f divergence without racing later commits.

findings.finding: The plan introduces a third exit code distinct from PASS and FAIL for the ERROR outcome, changing the verifier's exit-code contract, but does not acknowledge existing automation consumers of the current two-code contract (scripts that treat any non-PASS/non-zero exit as FAIL/refutation) nor state a migration or expand path for them.
findings.location: Fix step 2: 'exit code distinct from FAIL (gate refusal) so automation can retry/re-verify' and AC line 1 'distinct exit code'
scenarios: Existing CI/automation that branches on exit code 0=PASS, non-zero=FAIL will now see the new ERROR code and misclassify a retryable pathology as a hard refutation — the exact operator-steering-to-force problem the plan aims to fix could recur in unmigrated consumers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note listing the concrete numeric exit codes (PASS/FAIL/ERROR) and an AC asserting the FAIL code is unchanged so legacy consumers that only distinguish PASS-vs-nonzero still behave correctly, plus a line on how retry-aware consumers detect the ERROR code.
